intent.raw_query: Portugal Algarve, $2200, beach holiday with wine tasting, September 2026 from London

selected_hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for swimming and snorkeling among golden rock formations.

experiences.name: Algarve Wine & Vineyard Tour
experiences.description: Visit local Algarve wineries in the Lagoa DOC wine region, sampling indigenous varieties like Negra Mole and Crato Branco. Guided tours typically include cellar visits, barrel tastings, and paired local cheeses and charcuterie with stunning countryside views.

experiences.name: Benagil Sea Cave Kayak Tour
experiences.description: Paddle through the iconic Benagil Cave, one of the world's most beautiful sea caves, accessible only by water. A guided kayak tour takes you through hidden grottos, arched rock formations, and secret beaches along the dramatic Algarve coastline.

experiences.name: Ria Formosa Natural Park Boat & Beach Day
experiences.description: Take a traditional boat through the Ria Formosa lagoon system, stopping at barrier island beaches like Ilha Deserta and Ilha do Farol. Enjoy pristine, calm-water beaches, spot flamingos and migratory birds, and sample fresh oysters harvested directly from the lagoon.

experiences.name: Tavira Old Town Wine & Tapas Evening
experiences.description: Stroll through the charming historic streets of Tavira and join a guided wine and petiscos (Portuguese tapas) tour. Sample regional Alentejo and Algarve wines paired with local specialties like cataplana seafood stew, presunto ham, and almond-based sweets in intimate local tascas.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Portugal Algarve
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Faro Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Collect luggage, arrange ground transport (bus or shared shuttle to Lagoa area, ~€10-15), and check in to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay.
day_by_day.afternoon: After settling in, take a short walk down to Praia da Marinha beach (one of the Algarve's most iconic beaches, ~10 min walk from most accommodations in the area). Explore the dramatic golden limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear water. Swim if energy allows — September water is warm (~22°C).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll into the village of Carvoeiro or Lagoa town for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the waterfront and get your bearings.

meals.breakfast: Grab a quick pastel de nata and coffee at the airport or a café near the bus stop (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Pick up a fresh baguette sandwich or snacks from a local mini-market near the accommodation (~€4-6)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barradas in Lagoa or a simple tasca (local tavern) in Carvoeiro — try grilled sardines or piri-piri chicken with house wine (~€10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Book ground transport from Faro Airport in advance if possible. Eva Bus or Rede Expressos serve the Lagoa/Carvoeiro area. Taxi is ~€40-50. September is still peak-shoulder season — beaches will be quieter than August but still lovely.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning visit to Praia da Marinha at sunrise for a peaceful walk along the clifftop trail (Percurso dos Sete Vales Suspensos — Seven Hanging Valleys Trail starts nearby). Walk the first section east toward Benagil for stunning coastal views. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the clifftop walk or take a local bus/taxi to Praia de Benagil. Join an affordable kayak or paddleboard tour to explore the famous Benagil Sea Cave from the water (~€15-25 per person). Book on-site or via local operators at the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Praia da Marinha area. Relax at the accommodation. Walk to Carvoeiro village for sunset drinks on the beach terrace.

meals.breakfast: Coffee and toast at a local café in Lagoa or Carvoeiro (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local market — bread, local cheese, olives, fruit (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: O Castelo restaurant in Carvoeiro or a beachfront snack bar (marisqueira) — grilled fish of the day with salad and local wine (~€12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Seven Hanging Valleys Trail is one of the most beautiful free coastal walks in Europe. Wear sturdy shoes and bring water and sunscreen. Benagil cave kayak tours fill up quickly — arrive early or book ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Take a local bus or drive to Silves, the medieval Moorish capital of the Algarve (~20 min from Lagoa). Visit the impressive red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) — entrance ~€3. Explore the old town, cobblestone streets, and the Gothic cathedral (Sé de Silves) for free.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia in Silves (~€2 entry) to learn about the region's Moorish history. Walk along the Arade River banks and browse the local market stalls. Head back toward Lagoa and stop at a local winery or wine cooperative for an afternoon visit.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Adega do Cantor (owned by Cliff Richard) or Quinta dos Vales near Estômbar for a budget wine tasting session (~€8-15 per person including 3-4 wines). Book ahead for best rates.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria in Lagoa — coffee, orange juice, and a croissant (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Tasca do Zé in Silves or a local café near the castle — cataplana (traditional seafood stew) or bifana sandwich (~€8-12 per person)
meals.dinner: Simple home-style dinner at a tasca in Lagoa town — soup, main, dessert, and wine (menu do dia ~€9-12 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Silves is easily reached by bus from Lagoa (EVA Bus). The castle and cathedral are very close together — allow 2-3 hours total. Check winery opening hours and booking requirements before visiting.

day_by_day.morning: Beach day at Praia de Albandeira, a small hidden cove just east of Praia da Marinha (~15 min walk along the cliffs or a short drive). Arrive early to secure a good spot. Swim, snorkel, and enjoy the sheltered calm waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or bus to Armação de Pêra, a larger beach town nearby. Stroll along the long sandy beach (one of the longest in the Algarve). Visit the small whitewashed chapel of Nossa Senhora da Rocha perched on the clifftop headland — free entry, great views.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy the sunset from the cliffs at Nossa Senhora da Rocha. Head into Armação de Pêra for dinner at one of the seafront restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Grab groceries from a local supermarket (Pingo Doce in Lagoa) for a self-catered beach breakfast — yogurt, fruit, bread (~€3-5)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia de Albandeira or packed lunch from supermarket (~€5-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Tesouro do Mar in Armação de Pêra — fresh grilled fish, salad, local wine (~€13-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia de Albandeira is smaller and less crowded than Marinha — great for snorkeling. Bring your own snorkel gear if possible to save rental costs. The cliff walk between the beaches is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip by bus to Lagos (~45 min from Lagoa, ~€4-6 round trip). Explore the charming historic old town — Praça Gil Eanes, the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos, ~€3), and the Igreja de Santo António (free with museum ticket).
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short taxi to Ponta da Piedade — dramatic golden rock formations, grottos, and sea stacks. Free to visit. Optionally hire a local fisherman's boat from Lagos marina for a 45-min cave tour (~€10-15 per person). Explore Praia Dona Ana and Praia do Camilo (clifftop staircase access, free).
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Lagos's lively but affordable restaurant scene before busing back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Café Glória or any pastelaria in Lagos old town — coffee and pastel de nata (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: A Forja restaurant in Lagos or a takeaway from the municipal market — fresh seafood or grilled chicken (~€9-13 per person)
meals.dinner: O Camões tasca in Lagos old town — traditional Portuguese menu with house wine (~€10-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Lagos is one of the most popular towns in the Algarve — arrive early to beat crowds at Ponta da Piedade. The cliff walks between Dona Ana and Camilo beaches are free and stunning. Last bus back to Lagoa area departs around 20:00-21:00 — check EVA Bus schedule.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha. Rent a kayak or SUP board from local operators on the beach (~€10-15/hour) and paddle through the sea arches and caves accessible from the beach. Best done in calm morning conditions.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Lagoa town's local wine cooperative — Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa — for a budget-friendly tasting of local Algarvian wines, including the region's lesser-known reds and whites (~€5-10 for tasting). Browse the cooperative's shop for affordable bottles to take back.
day_by_day.evening: Self-catered evening at the accommodation using local market finds — wine, cheese, charcuterie, olives, fresh bread. Enjoy on the terrace or balcony.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — bread, local honey, coffee (~€2-3 from supermarket)
meals.lunch: Snack bar near Praia da Marinha or packed lunch (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Self-catered charcuterie and wine board from Pingo Doce or local market — great value at ~€8-12 for two people

day_by_day.notes: The Adega Cooperativa de Lagoa is one of the most authentic and affordable wine tasting experiences in the Algarve. Call ahead to confirm opening hours. September kayaking conditions are usually excellent — calm seas and warm water.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Portimão and Praia da Rocha (~20 min by bus from Lagoa, ~€3-4). Visit the Museu de Portimão (free on Sunday, €3 other days) — a fascinating museum built inside a former fish canning factory. Explore the riverside market area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk or take a short bus to Praia da Rocha — a wide, dramatic sandy beach backed by red cliffs. Swim and relax. Walk along the beachfront promenade. Optionally take a boat trip from Portimão marina to explore the coastline (~€15-20 per person).
day_by_day.evening: Dine in Portimão before returning to Lagoa. Portimão is famous for its charcoal-grilled sardines — try them fresh from a riverside grill.

meals.breakfast: Café in Portimão town center — galão (milky coffee) and toast (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or snack bar at Praia da Rocha (~€6-9)
meals.dinner: Tasca do Celso or any riverside sardine grill in Portimão — grilled sardines, bread, salad, and wine (~€10-13 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Portimão's riverside area is famous for its sardine grilling culture — the smell of charcoal and sardines is unmissable. The Museu de Portimão is genuinely excellent and very affordable. Check bus return times to Lagoa.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the inland Algarve — take a bus or local taxi to Monchique, a mountain village in the Serra de Monchique (~45 min from Portimão/Lagoa area). Walk through the charming village, visit the ruined Franciscan convent, and sample local medronho (arbutus berry firewater) at a local shop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike or take a taxi up to Fóia, the highest peak in the Algarve (902m) — panoramic views over the entire coast on a clear day. Free to visit. Walk back down part of the way through eucalyptus and cork oak forest. Return to Lagoa by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening in Carvoeiro — sunset walk on the beach, then dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Café in Monchique village — coffee and local corn bread (~€3)
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique — hearty mountain food like carne de porco à alentejana (pork and clams) or grilled chicken (~€10-13 per person)
meals.dinner: A Tasca do Pescador in Carvoeiro or similar local tasca — grilled fish or meat with local wine (~€11-15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is a refreshing change from the coastal heat — temperatures can be 5-8°C cooler than the coast. The medronho firewater makes a great and very affordable souvenir (~€5-8 for a bottle). Check bus connections carefully as services to Monchique can be limited.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Praia do Carvalho, a hidden gem just west of Praia da Marinha — accessible via a short tunnel carved through the cliff. Arrive early to enjoy it nearly alone. Swim in the sheltered cove and explore the rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Quinta dos Vales winery near Estômbar (close to Lagoa) — a well-regarded estate offering affordable guided tours and tastings (~€10-15 per person). The estate also has sculpture gardens. Book ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset at Praia da Marinha viewpoint — one of the most photographed spots in Portugal. Bring a bottle of local wine from the winery visit for a perfect picnic sunset.

meals.breakfast: Local padaria (bakery) in Lagoa — fresh bread rolls and coffee (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Packed picnic at Praia do Carvalho — bread, cheese, fruit, olives from supermarket (~€5-7)
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Barradas in Lagoa — traditional Algarvian cuisine, house wine, great value (~€11-14 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Praia do Carvalho is accessed through a narrow tunnel — bring a small torch/phone light. The beach gets crowded by midday in September. Quinta dos Vales is one of the most accessible wineries to Praia da Marinha and offers excellent value tastings.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Faro, the Algarve's capital (~45 min by bus from Lagoa, ~€5-7 round trip). Explore the beautiful walled old town (Cidade Velha) — Arco da Vila, the Sé Cathedral (rooftop views ~€3.50), and the charming cobbled streets.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Carmo and the famous Bone Chapel (Capela dos Ossos) in Faro (~€4 entry) — a striking and unique attraction. Stroll along the marina and Jardim Manuel Bivar. Take the ferry to Ilha de Faro (Faro Beach) for a late afternoon swim (~€2.50 round trip) — part of the Ria Formosa Natural Park.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Faro old town before the bus back to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Pastelaria Gardy in Faro — historic café, coffee and pastries (~€3-4)
meals.lunch: Mercado Municipal de Faro food stalls — fresh local food at market prices (~€7-10)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Cidade Velha in Faro old town — traditional Portuguese cuisine in a historic setting (~€12-16 per person)

day_by_day.notes: The Bone Chapel in Faro is genuinely fascinating and not to be missed. The ferry to Ilha de Faro runs regularly and the beach is beautiful and less crowded than the main Algarve beaches. Check last bus time back to Lagoa.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach relaxation day at Praia da Marinha. Spend the morning swimming, sunbathing, and exploring the rock pools at low tide. September light is golden and beautiful — great for photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Walk the western section of the Seven Hanging Valleys Trail toward Praia de Vale Centeanes and Praia do Carvoeiro. The trail passes through dramatic clifftop scenery with views of sea stacks and arches. Free to walk.
day_by_day.evening: Final wine tasting evening — visit a local wine bar or restaurant in Carvoeiro with a good Algarvian wine list. Try wines from the Lagoa DOC region — local whites are particularly good.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — coffee, fruit, yogurt (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Beach snack bar at Praia da Marinha or Carvoeiro — prego sandwich and cold beer (~€7-9)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Boneca in Carvoeiro or similar — fresh catch of the day, local wine (~€13-17 per person)

day_by_day.notes: This is a great day to slow down, reflect on the trip, and enjoy the natural beauty of Praia da Marinha at a relaxed pace. The clifftop walk at golden hour is magical. September evenings are warm enough to eat outside comfortably.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Algar Seco rock formations near Carvoeiro — a dramatic landscape of sculpted limestone rocks, natural pools, and sea tunnels. Free to visit and walk around. Bring a swimsuit to swim in the natural rock pools.
day_by_day.afternoon: Final winery visit — Herdade dos Grous or another nearby estate for a last tasting session. Alternatively, visit the local market in Lagoa (held on weekdays) to pick up souvenirs — local honey, fig jam, medronho, almond sweets (amêndoa), and local wines at supermarket prices.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner — splurge slightly on a nicer restaurant for the last evening. Enjoy a cataplana (traditional copper pot seafood stew) — the signature dish of the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Café in Carvoeiro — coffee, fresh orange juice, toast with local butter and jam (~€4-5)
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café near Algar Seco — soup and sandwich (~€6-8)
meals.dinner: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira or a quality cataplana restaurant in Carvoeiro — cataplana for two, local wine, dessert (~€18-22 per person as a farewell treat)

day_by_day.notes: Algar Seco is a 10-15 min walk from Carvoeiro beach — wear shoes with grip as the rocks can be slippery. The local market in Lagoa is a great place to find authentic, affordable souvenirs. Pack your bags tonight for an easier morning departure.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at Praia da Marinha — one last sunrise walk along the cliffs. Take in the views, breathe the sea air, and say goodbye to one of Portugal's most beautiful coastlines. Check out of accommodation.
day_by_day.afternoon: Transfer to Faro Airport for departure. Allow 2-2.5 hours before flight for check-in. Bus from Lagoa to Faro takes ~45-60 min (EVA Bus, ~€5-7). Alternatively, book a shared shuttle (~€12-15 per person) for convenience.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport.

meals.breakfast: Final pastel de nata and coffee at a café in Lagoa before checkout (~€2-3)
meals.lunch: Snack or light meal at Faro Airport or a café near the bus station (~€6-10)
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight

day_by_day.notes: Check bus times from Lagoa to Faro the evening before to ensure you catch the right connection. Faro Airport is small and manageable but can get busy — arrive with plenty of time. Consider buying a few bottles of local Lagoa DOC wine at the airport duty-free as final souvenirs.

trip_options.title: Classic Portugal Algarve Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrival – no activities scheduled before 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and rent a car (recommended for the Algarve). Drive ~45 minutes west to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa and check in to the Boutique Stay. Freshen up and take a gentle first stroll down to Praia da Marinha viewpoint to soak in the dramatic golden limestone cliffs and turquoise water.
day_by_day.evening: Head into the village of Carvoeiro (10 min drive) for a relaxed first dinner. Explore the pretty whitewashed streets and the small beach cove at sunset.

meals.breakfast: Snack at Faro Airport before or after landing
meals.lunch: Light bite at a café near Faro Airport or grab takeaway pastéis de nata for the road
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro – mid-range Portuguese seafood and grills with sea views; expect €20–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Pick up a Portuguese SIM card or activate roaming at the airport. Car rental is strongly recommended for this itinerary. September weather in the Algarve is typically warm and sunny (24–28 °C).

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely Portuguese breakfast at the boutique stay, hike the stunning coastal trail from Praia da Marinha to Benagil (approx. 3 km one way). Admire the sea caves, rock arches and hidden coves along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Benagil Beach, join a kayak or SUP tour into the famous Benagil Sea Cave (Algar de Benagil) – one of Portugal's most iconic natural wonders. Book in advance as tours fill up quickly in September. Return to the hotel for a mid-afternoon rest.
day_by_day.evening: Drive to Lagoa town (15 min) for a relaxed evening stroll and dinner in the local square.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay – fresh bread, local cheese, fruit and coffee
meals.lunch: Snack bar at Benagil Beach – grilled sardine sandwich or bifanas (pork rolls) with a cold Sagres beer; €8–12
meals.dinner: Restaurante Mirandus in Lagoa – traditional Algarvian cuisine, cataplana de peixe (fish stew), local wine; €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Benagil kayak tours typically run 1–1.5 hours and cost €20–35 per person. Book the evening before or online in advance. Wear water shoes and bring sunscreen.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Armação de Pêra (20 min). Walk along the long sandy beach – one of the Algarve's longest – and visit the small 17th-century fortress chapel at the western tip of the beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Silves region (30 min drive inland) for a wine tasting experience. Visit Quinta dos Vales or Adega do Cantor (Cliff Richard's famous winery) – both offer guided tours and tastings of Algarve DOC wines amid scenic vineyards. Book ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the historic town of Silves. Walk up to the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) for golden-hour views over the Arade River and orange groves.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Light tapas and wine at the vineyard during the tasting experience (often included in the tour)
meals.dinner: Restaurante Marisqueira Rui in Silves – beloved local institution famous for cataplana and fresh seafood; €22–32 per person

day_by_day.notes: Quinta dos Vales wine tours cost approximately €15–25 per person including tasting. Silves Castle entry is around €3. Try the local medronho (arbutus berry spirit) if offered.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a relaxed beach morning at Praia de Albandeira – a small, sheltered and relatively uncrowded cove just minutes from the hotel. Ideal for snorkelling along the rocky edges. Bring your own snorkel gear or rent locally.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west to Portimão (25 min) and visit the Museu de Portimão – a free/low-cost museum set in a former sardine canning factory, offering fascinating insight into the region's fishing heritage. Afterwards, walk along the Portimão riverside promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Portimão for the evening. The waterfront area has lively bars and restaurants. Catch the sunset from the riverside.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Pack a picnic from the local Lagoa market or supermarket and enjoy it on Albandeira beach
meals.dinner: Taberna da Maré in Portimão – casual, authentic grilled fish and seafood on the riverside; €18–26 per person. Try the famous Portimão grilled sardines.

day_by_day.notes: Museu de Portimão is closed on Mondays. Entry is free on the last Sunday of each month. Albandeira beach has limited parking – arrive early or walk down from the road.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Praia da Rocha (10 min from Portimão) – a wide, dramatic beach backed by colourful cliffs and a 16th-century fortress (Fortaleza de Santa Catarina). Explore the fortress and enjoy the panoramic views over the Arade River mouth.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive further west to Alvor (15 min). Wander through the charming whitewashed village and its 16th-century Manueline church. Then walk or cycle along the Alvor Estuary Boardwalk through the natural reserve – flamingos and herons are often spotted in September.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Alvor's lively but charming restaurant strip for dinner, then drive back to the hotel (30 min).

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Cervejaria Valentim in Alvor – local favourite for fresh clams (ameijoas à Bulhão Pato) and grilled fish; €16–22 per person
meals.dinner: O Barão in Alvor – cosy mid-range restaurant with excellent grilled meats and local wines; €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Alvor Estuary boardwalk is flat and easy – great for a gentle afternoon walk. Bring binoculars if you have them for birdwatching. Fortaleza de Santa Catarina is free to enter.

day_by_day.morning: Full beach day at Meia Praia – a vast, 4 km stretch of golden sand east of Lagos (35 min drive). Arrive early to secure a good spot. The water is calmer here than the Atlantic-facing beaches, ideal for swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive into Lagos town (10 min from Meia Praia). Explore the historic old town: the Slave Market Museum (Mercado de Escravos), the golden baroque interior of Igreja de Santo António, and the medieval city walls. Walk along the Ponta da Piedade cliffs for spectacular rock formations.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner – the town has a buzzing Sunday evening atmosphere with street musicians and a great mix of restaurants.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Snack bar on Meia Praia beach – grilled fish, salads and cold drinks; €12–18
meals.dinner: Restaurante Adega da Marina in Lagos – traditional Portuguese cuisine in a rustic wine cellar setting; €22–30 per person. Try the arroz de lingueirão (razor clam rice).

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon light. If time allows, take a 45-minute boat tour from Lagos marina to see the caves and grottos at Ponta da Piedade (€15–20). Book at the marina on arrival.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recharge morning. Enjoy a slow breakfast at the boutique stay and take a leisurely swim or sunbathe at Praia da Marinha. Read, relax and enjoy the stunning surroundings with no rush.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Porches (20 min) to visit the famous Porches Pottery (Olaria Algarve) – the iconic blue-and-white hand-painted ceramics workshop. Browse the showroom and watch artisans at work. Pick up unique souvenirs. Then visit a local cooperative wine producer – Adega Cooperativa do Algarve in Lagoa – for a tasting of regional wines.
day_by_day.evening: Quiet evening near the hotel. Walk down to Praia da Marinha at dusk for a spectacular golden-hour view of the cliffs.

meals.breakfast: Extended breakfast at the boutique stay – treat yourself to fresh orange juice and local pastries
meals.lunch: Restaurante O Leão de Porches – a beloved local restaurant known for hearty Algarvian home cooking; €15–22 per person
meals.dinner: In-room or self-catered evening – pick up local cheeses, presunto, olives, fresh bread and a bottle of Algarve wine from a local supermarket; ~€15–20 for two

day_by_day.notes: Porches Pottery is a must for ceramic lovers – prices range from €5 for small pieces to €80+ for large decorative plates. The Lagoa wine cooperative offers tastings for approximately €5–10 per person.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Albufeira (30 min). Visit the old town – the original whitewashed fishing village above the main tourist strip – and the smaller, more authentic Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) where local boats still land their catch in the morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a dolphin watching boat tour from Albufeira marina (2–2.5 hours). Common dolphins and bottlenose dolphins are frequently seen in September. Book at the marina or in advance online.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Albufeira's old town at night – it comes alive with street performers, bars and restaurants. Enjoy the atmosphere before driving back.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante A Ruína in Albufeira – iconic cliffside restaurant with fantastic sea views and fresh seafood; €22–30 per person
meals.dinner: Tasca do Viegas in Albufeira old town – charming local tasca with petiscos (Portuguese tapas) and regional wines; €18–24 per person

day_by_day.notes: Dolphin watching tours cost approximately €35–45 per person. September is an excellent month for sightings. The drive back to Praia da Marinha from Albufeira is about 30 minutes – plan to leave by 21:00.

day_by_day.morning: Drive east to Vilamoura (40 min). Walk around the glamorous marina – one of Europe's largest – and visit the Roman ruins of Cerro da Vila, a well-preserved 1st-century Roman settlement with mosaics, baths and a small museum right next to the marina.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Quarteira Beach (5 min from Vilamoura) – a long, wide sandy beach popular with locals. Enjoy a swim and a relaxing afternoon. Alternatively, if interested, Vilamoura has world-class golf courses (book in advance; green fees €60–120).
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Vilamoura marina with its array of mid-range to upscale restaurants and lively waterfront atmosphere. Drive back to the hotel.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Aqui Há Peixe in Quarteira – a local favourite away from the tourist strip, excellent grilled fish by weight; €18–25 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurante Borda d'Água at Vilamoura Marina – fresh seafood and grills with marina views; €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Cerro da Vila Roman ruins entry is approximately €3. Vilamoura marina is very walkable. Parking is available near the marina. Drive back to Praia da Marinha is approximately 40 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Faro (50 min) for a half-day city exploration. Visit the Faro Old Town (Cidade Velha) within the medieval walls: the Gothic-Baroque Faro Cathedral (Sé de Faro) with its rooftop terrace offering panoramic views, and the haunting Carmo Church with its famous Chapel of Bones.
day_by_day.afternoon: From Faro harbour, take a ferry or boat tour into the Ria Formosa Natural Park – a stunning lagoon system of islands, salt marshes and tidal flats. Visit the barrier islands of Ilha Deserta or Ilha da Culatra for pristine, uncrowded beaches and crystal-clear water.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Faro for dinner in the old town before the drive back.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: O Castelo restaurant on Ilha Deserta (if visiting) – fresh seafood in a remote, beautiful setting; €20–30 per person. Or pack a picnic for the island.
meals.dinner: Restaurante Faz Gostos in Faro old town – creative Algarvian cuisine in a charming historic setting; €22–30 per person

day_by_day.notes: Faro Cathedral tower entry ~€3.50. Ria Formosa ferry to Ilha Deserta costs ~€10–15 return. The natural park is a birdwatcher's paradise – flamingos, spoonbills and kingfishers are common in September. Drive back to hotel is 50 minutes.

day_by_day.morning: Drive west for a full day in the western Algarve. Start at Sagres (1 hour 15 min drive). Visit the dramatic Fortaleza de Sagres – the windswept promontory fortress associated with Henry the Navigator, with stunning Atlantic views. Walk to Ponta de Sagres for dramatic cliff-edge scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive 6 km to Cabo de São Vicente – the most south-westerly point of continental Europe. Stand at the edge of the continent and watch the Atlantic swells crash against the cliffs. Visit the lighthouse. Then relax at Praia do Beliche – a sheltered cove near Sagres with wild, dramatic scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Have dinner in Sagres village before the scenic drive back east.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay – pack an early breakfast or grab pastries en route
meals.lunch: Restaurante Nortada in Sagres – casual, excellent fresh fish and seafood with views of Sagres Bay; €18–25 per person
meals.dinner: A Tasca in Sagres – beloved local restaurant, outstanding grilled fish and cataplana; €20–28 per person

day_by_day.notes: Fortaleza de Sagres entry ~€3. Cabo de São Vicente is free. The drive from Praia da Marinha to Sagres is scenic – allow 1h15m. This is a long day with driving – depart by 08:30 to make the most of it. Return drive approximately 1h15m.

day_by_day.morning: Final full beach day – return to your favourite beach or explore Praia do Carvalho (a hidden gem near the hotel, accessible via a tunnel through the cliff). Pack snorkelling gear and enjoy the last morning in the crystalline Algarve waters.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive inland to Monchique (45 min) – a charming mountain village in the Serra de Monchique. Visit the ruined Franciscan convent (Convento de Nossa Senhora do Desterro), stroll the pretty streets, and sample the local medronho firewater and smoked Monchique ham (presunto). Drive up to Fóia peak (902m) – the highest point in the Algarve – for sweeping panoramic views over the entire region.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Carvoeiro or Lagoa for a special farewell dinner to celebrate the trip.

meals.breakfast: At the boutique stay
meals.lunch: Restaurante Central in Monchique – rustic mountain cooking, hearty bean stews, grilled chouriço and presunto; €14–20 per person
meals.dinner: Restaurante O Escondidinho in Carvoeiro – excellent farewell dinner spot with a terrace, creative Algarvian cuisine and a strong local wine list; €25–35 per person

day_by_day.notes: Monchique is noticeably cooler than the coast – bring a light layer. The drive up to Fóia has some winding roads but is accessible by normal car. Medronho can be purchased directly from local producers in Monchique – a great gift to bring home.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely breakfast at the boutique stay. Take one last walk down to Praia da Marinha viewpoint to say goodbye to the spectacular cliffs. Pack and check out.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Faro Airport (allow 50 minutes plus buffer). Return the rental car. Depending on your departure time, browse the airport shops for last-minute Portuguese wine, port, tinned fish (conservas) and pastéis de nata to bring home.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Faro Airport. Carry wonderful memories of 13 days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final breakfast at the boutique stay – savour the last Portuguese coffee and local pastries
meals.lunch: Light meal at Faro Airport or a final pastel de nata at a café near the airport
meals.dinner: On the flight or at your destination

day_by_day.notes: Return your rental car at least 2 hours before departure. Faro Airport is small and manageable but can be busy on Sundays in September. Check your airline's luggage allowance if purchasing wine or ceramics to bring home. Consider shipping fragile ceramics via a courier service arranged at Porches Pottery.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Portugal Algarve Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim
experiences.description: Explore one of the Algarve's most stunning beaches, known for its dramatic limestone cliffs, sea caves, and crystal-clear turquoise waters. Hike the clifftop trail from Benagil and descend to the secluded cove for swimming and snorkeling among golden rock formations.

day_by_day.morning: Flight arrival — no activities scheduled before 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Faro Airport at 13:00. Private transfer arranged to Praia da Marinha, Lagoa Boutique Stay (~45 min scenic drive). Check in, settle into your luxury suite, and enjoy a welcome drink on the terrace overlooking the Atlantic. Take a leisurely stroll down to Praia da Marinha beach (5-min walk) to get your first glimpse of the iconic golden limestone cliffs and crystalline waters.
day_by_day.evening: Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed first dinner at a top local restaurant in Carvoeiro or Lagoa — a gentle introduction to Algarvian cuisine without venturing far from the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Enjoyed on the plane or at the airport
meals.lunch: Light welcome snack / charcuterie board arranged by the boutique hotel upon arrival
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante O Castelo in Carvoeiro — renowned for fresh grilled fish, cataplana seafood stew, and an excellent Portuguese wine list. Reserve a terrace table for sunset views.

day_by_day.notes: Request early check-in when booking if the flight schedule allows luggage drop-off. Private airport transfer recommended for a seamless luxury start. Pack light beach essentials for the afternoon stroll.

day_by_day.morning: After a leisurely breakfast at the hotel, embark on the Praia da Marinha Coastal Hike & Swim — one of the Algarve's most celebrated coastal walks. Follow the clifftop trail revealing dramatic sea caves, natural arches, and hidden grottoes. Descend to the beach for a refreshing swim in the turquoise waters. Bring snorkelling gear to explore the underwater rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for a poolside lunch. Spend the afternoon on a private boat tour departing from Benagil (15 min drive), exploring the famous Benagil Sea Cave, hidden grottos, and secluded beaches only accessible by water. Opt for a premium catamaran or RIB speedboat charter for exclusivity.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitivo on the hotel terrace with local sparkling wines (Espumante). Dinner at a fine dining restaurant in Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Full Portuguese breakfast at the hotel — fresh pastries, local cheeses, presunto, fresh-squeezed orange juice, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Poolside lunch at the hotel — grilled sea bass, salads, and chilled Vinho Verde
meals.dinner: Dinner at Bombordo Restaurant, Carvoeiro — creative modern Portuguese cuisine with panoramic ocean views and an award-winning wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Book the Benagil boat tour in advance — September remains busy. Wear reef-safe sunscreen for the swim. The coastal hike is moderate difficulty; wear proper footwear for cliff paths.

day_by_day.morning: Morning wine tasting experience at Adega do Cantor (Guia, ~20 min drive) — the celebrated winery co-founded by Sir Cliff Richard. Enjoy a guided tour of the estate, vineyard walk, and a curated tasting of their signature Vida Nova and Onda Nova wines paired with local charcuterie and cheeses.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Silves (~30 min) — the ancient Moorish capital of the Algarve. Visit the magnificent red sandstone Silves Castle (Castelo de Silves) and the Gothic Cathedral. Explore the charming old town, browse artisan shops, and visit the Museu Municipal de Arqueologia.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the Lagoa area for a refined dinner showcasing the region's cataplana tradition.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — local honey, almond pastries, fresh fruit, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Wine estate lunch pairing at Adega do Cantor — curated tasting menu with wine pairings on the vineyard terrace
meals.dinner: Dinner at Marisqueira Rui in Silves — legendary seafood restaurant famed for its cataplana de marisco and fresh lobster, beloved by locals and celebrities alike

day_by_day.notes: Book the Adega do Cantor tasting experience in advance. Silves is best explored on foot — wear comfortable walking shoes. September evenings are warm; light layers recommended.

day_by_day.morning: Private yoga or wellness session on the hotel terrace or beach at sunrise, arranged through the boutique stay. Follow with a relaxed morning at Praia da Marinha — find a quiet cove and enjoy the beach at its most peaceful before day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive west to Praia da Rocha (Portimão, ~25 min) — one of the Algarve's grandest beaches with dramatic cliff formations. Rent a premium sun lounger at a beach club and enjoy the broader expanse of golden sand. Explore the clifftop promenade and the fortress of Santa Catarina.
day_by_day.evening: Portimão evening — stroll along the marina, browse the waterfront, and dine at one of the city's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast with fresh local almond croissants and regional fruit
meals.lunch: Beach club lunch at Praia da Rocha — fresh seafood, grilled octopus salad, and chilled rosé
meals.dinner: Dinner at Caniço Restaurant, Portimão — perched dramatically on the cliffs above Praia da Rocha with exceptional seafood and Portuguese wine selection

day_by_day.notes: Praia da Rocha can be crowded in September afternoons — arrive by 14:00 to secure premium beach club spots. The clifftop walk at sunset is spectacular.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Lagos (~35 min drive west). Morning exploration of the historic old town — visit the Igreja de Santo António (a baroque masterpiece), the Slave Market Museum, and the beautifully tiled Praça Gil Eanes. Walk the ancient city walls.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Ponta da Piedade — Lagos's most iconic natural landmark. Hire a private kayak or stand-up paddleboard guide to explore the extraordinary golden rock arches, sea stacks, and hidden grottos from the water level. Swim in the sheltered lagoons between the formations.
day_by_day.evening: Stay in Lagos for dinner — the town has a vibrant evening atmosphere with excellent dining options.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh pastries, smoked salmon, local cheeses, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at No Pátio Restaurant, Lagos — charming courtyard setting with refined Portuguese cuisine and excellent local wines
meals.dinner: Dinner at Adega da Marina, Lagos — beloved institution for traditional Algarvian cuisine, grilled fish, and an extensive Portuguese wine list in a rustic-elegant setting

day_by_day.notes: Ponta da Piedade is best visited in the afternoon when the light illuminates the golden cliffs most dramatically. Book kayak guide in advance for Saturday. Lagos old town is walkable — park at the marina.

day_by_day.morning: Leisurely hotel morning — sleep in, enjoy an extended breakfast, and have a spa treatment (massage or facial) if available at the boutique stay or a nearby luxury spa. Alternatively, take a gentle morning swim at Praia da Marinha.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Ferragudo (~20 min) — one of the Algarve's most picturesque and authentic fishing villages. Explore the charming whitewashed village, visit the 16th-century Castelo de São João de Arade overlooking the Arade River estuary, and browse the small artisan galleries. Take a short boat ride across to Portimão marina.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a clifftop bar in Ferragudo, then dinner in the village.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury hotel breakfast — full spread with eggs cooked to order, local smoked fish, pastries, and fresh juices
meals.lunch: Casual waterfront lunch in Ferragudo at Restaurante Sueste — legendary for fresh grilled fish and seafood with views over the Arade River
meals.dinner: Dinner at Restaurante A Tasca, Ferragudo — intimate, highly regarded restaurant with market-driven Portuguese cuisine and superb wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Sunday in Ferragudo is particularly charming — locals gather at the waterfront. The village is small and best explored slowly on foot. Reservations strongly recommended at A Tasca.

day_by_day.morning: Premium wine tour of the Algarve interior — visit Quinta dos Vales (Estômbar, ~25 min drive), a prestigious wine estate with an extraordinary outdoor sculpture garden. Enjoy a guided vineyard tour, cellar visit, and premium wine tasting of their award-winning reds and whites, including the flagship Earl of Déville range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to the Ria Formosa Natural Park area (drive east ~1.5 hrs) for a different coastal landscape. Take a boat tour through the stunning lagoon system, visiting barrier islands and spotting flamingos, spoonbills, and other migratory birds. Swim at pristine Ilha Deserta (Desert Island) — accessible only by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Drive back to Lagoa. Relaxed evening at the hotel with room service or a quiet dinner nearby.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light and energising ahead of the wine estate visit
meals.lunch: Vineyard lunch at Quinta dos Vales — gourmet estate lunch with wine pairings on the terrace overlooking the vines
meals.dinner: In-room dining or light dinner at a nearby Lagoa restaurant — Restaurante Atlântico in Carvoeiro for fresh seafood and local wines

day_by_day.notes: Book Quinta dos Vales tasting and lunch well in advance — it's a premium experience. The Ria Formosa boat tour is a full afternoon; bring a hat, sunscreen, and camera. September is excellent for birdwatching.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure at Praia da Marinha. Hire a stand-up paddleboard or sea kayak from a local provider and explore the coastline independently. The September sea is warm and calm — perfect for paddling into sea caves and around rock formations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Albufeira (~30 min east) for an afternoon of exploration. Visit the charming old town (Albufeira Velha) — a maze of whitewashed alleys, traditional ceramic shops, and the clifftop miradouro. Avoid the crowded tourist strip and focus on the authentic upper town. Visit Praia dos Pescadores (Fishermen's Beach) below the old town.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Albufeira at a top-rated restaurant before returning to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh fruit platter, yoghurt with local honey, pastries, and coffee
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at Praia da Marinha — hotel-arranged picnic basket with gourmet sandwiches, local cheeses, olives, and chilled wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Evaristo Restaurant, Albufeira — elegant clifftop restaurant with exceptional fresh fish, premium steaks, and one of the best wine lists in the Algarve

day_by_day.notes: The hotel can arrange a gourmet picnic basket with advance notice — highly recommended for the beach morning. Albufeira old town is best in the evening when day-trippers leave.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private golf experience at one of the Algarve's world-class courses — Vale da Pinta Golf Course (Carvoeiro, ~15 min drive) or Penina Hotel & Golf Resort (~30 min). Even for non-golfers, the manicured grounds, cork oak forests, and Atlantic views make for a spectacular morning walk. Alternatively, enjoy a luxury spa morning at Penina Resort.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the coast for an afternoon at Praia de Benagil — one of the Algarve's most photographed beaches. Swim, sunbathe, and take a short guided cliff walk to viewpoints above the famous Benagil Cave. Watch the afternoon light play on the golden cliffs.
day_by_day.evening: Elegant dinner at a Michelin-starred or highly acclaimed fine dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — full spread with freshly baked bread, local jams, eggs, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Clubhouse lunch at the golf course — grilled meats, salads, and cold Portuguese beer or wine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Ocean Restaurant, Vila Vita Parc (Porches, ~15 min drive) — two Michelin-starred, one of Portugal's finest dining experiences with tasting menus celebrating local ingredients and an extraordinary 35,000-bottle wine cellar

day_by_day.notes: Ocean Restaurant at Vila Vita Parc requires advance reservation — book weeks ahead for this unmissable Michelin experience. Smart dress code required. The golf course should also be booked in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Sagres (~1 hr west) — the dramatic southwestern tip of Europe. Visit Cabo de São Vicente, the most southwesterly point of continental Europe, where sheer 75-metre cliffs meet the Atlantic. The lighthouse and the raw, windswept landscape are unforgettable. Visit the imposing Fortaleza de Sagres (Sagres Fortress) with its mysterious wind compass.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the wild beaches around Sagres — Praia do Beliche (tucked beneath dramatic cliffs) and Praia da Mareta (sheltered and beautiful). The Atlantic swell here is stronger — ideal for watching surfers or simply experiencing the raw power of the ocean. Visit a local surf shop for the culture.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner in Sagres before the return drive to Lagoa.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — energising start for the longer drive day
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurante Bossa Nova, Sagres — excellent fresh fish and seafood in a relaxed setting beloved by locals
meals.dinner: Dinner at A Sagres Restaurant — charming local restaurant with outstanding grilled fish, seafood rice, and regional wines before the return drive

day_by_day.notes: Sagres can be windy even in September — bring a light jacket. The drive along the Vicentine Coast is spectacular; allow extra time for stops. Return drive to Lagoa is approximately 1 hour.

day_by_day.morning: Exclusive private wine and gastronomy tour of the Alentejo wine region (accessible as a day trip, ~1.5 hrs north of Lagoa). Visit Herdade do Esporão or Herdade dos Grous — two of Portugal's most prestigious wine estates. Enjoy guided vineyard tours, cellar visits, and a premium tasting of world-class Alentejo reds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring the Alentejo landscape — rolling plains of cork oak, olive groves, and vineyards. Visit the medieval walled village of Mértola or the Roman ruins at Milreu (if returning via Faro). The contrast with the coastal Algarve is remarkable.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Lagoa. Final evening at the hotel — relaxed dinner at a favourite local restaurant from the week.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — light and early ahead of the day trip
meals.lunch: Estate lunch at the Alentejo winery — a highlight of the trip; multi-course regional menu with wine pairings on the estate terrace
meals.dinner: Return dinner at Restaurante O Castelo, Carvoeiro — revisiting a favourite from Day 1 with new appreciation for Portuguese wine and cuisine

day_by_day.notes: Book the Alentejo wine estate experience well in advance — private tours with lunch are exclusive and limited. Consider hiring a private driver for this day to enjoy the wine tastings fully without driving concerns.

day_by_day.morning: Final beach morning at Praia da Marinha — savour the beach that has been your home base all week. Take a slow walk along the cliffs, swim in the coves, and photograph the limestone arches in the morning light. Collect sea glass or simply sit and absorb the beauty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Museu do Carvoeiro or explore the village of Carvoeiro in depth — browse the ceramic and azulejo shops, visit the clifftop chapel of Nossa Senhora do Desterro, and enjoy the village atmosphere. Alternatively, book a final premium spa treatment at a nearby luxury resort (Tivoli Carvoeiro or Monte Santo Resort).
day_by_day.evening: Grand farewell dinner — the finest meal of the trip at a celebrated restaurant to mark the penultimate evening.

meals.breakfast: Champagne breakfast on the hotel terrace — a special treat to mark the final full beach morning
meals.lunch: Lunch at a clifftop café in Carvoeiro — fresh salads, grilled fish, and a final glass of local white wine overlooking the sea
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Bon Bon Restaurant, Carvoeiro (Michelin-starred) — Chef Louis Anjos's creative tasting menus celebrate Algarve produce with extraordinary finesse; reserve the chef's table for the ultimate experience

day_by_day.notes: Bon Bon holds a Michelin star and is one of the Algarve's most celebrated restaurants — book weeks in advance. Request the chef's table or a window table for the best experience. This is the gastronomic highlight of the trip.

day_by_day.morning: Final leisurely morning — last swim at Praia da Marinha or a gentle clifftop walk at sunrise. Pack and check out of the boutique stay. Arrange a private transfer to Faro Airport.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure from Faro Airport. If the flight is late afternoon, stop at a local market in Lagoa or Portimão for last-minute Portuguese souvenirs — local wines, artisan ceramics, almond sweets (Dom Rodrigos), carob products, and Flor de Sal sea salt.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry the memories of 13 extraordinary days in the Algarve.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy every last bite of the fresh pastries, local cheeses, and artisan coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at a café in Lagoa town or at Faro Airport departure lounge
meals.dinner: In-flight or at destination

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before departure for the Faro Airport transfer and check-in. Purchase local wines at a reputable wine shop in Lagoa before departure — Quinta dos Vales and Vida Nova bottles make excellent gifts. Confirm private transfer the evening before.
